members.name: readingsField
members.description: The field of each row holding its readings by time, and of the `c2-table-column` that is the time columns' template.

members.name: observations
members.description:
Readings as a flat list, sorted into the rows by `measure` (a row's key) and `time`. A reading of a measure no
row has is left out. An array in the property, JSON in the attribute.

members.name: times
members.description: Times shown even with no reading yet, `;`-separated in the attribute: the column of the next round.

members.name: timeOrder
members.description: `asc` (the default) puts the earliest time first, `desc` the newest.

members.name: timeFormat
members.description: How the headers write the times: `time` (the default, with the day over the first time of each day), `date`, `datetime` or `text`.

type.text: { inputs: unknown[]; byMeasure: Map<string, Record<string, unknown>> } | undefined

members.name: #series
members.default: new WeakMap<TableColumnConfig, { inputs: unknown[]; columns: TableColumnConfig[] }>()

members.name: addTime
members.description: Adds a column for `time` (an ISO time such as `2026-11-14T20:00`), in its place among the others.

members.name: expandColumns
members.description: The declared columns as the table draws them: a variant may stand several columns for one (`c2-flowsheet`).

members.name: readCell
members.description: A reading: the row's own (an edit lands there), else the observation of its measure at that time.

members.name: needsSort
members.description: Whether `changed` holds a property the rows are built from beyond those of a flat table.

members.name: #byMeasure
members.description: The observations by measure, then by time; kept while the list is the same.

members.name: #timeColumns
members.description: The columns the template stands for: one per time, kept while the rows and the template are the same.

members.name: groupBy
members.description:
Groups the rows by these fields, outermost first: `group-by="region,status"` in the attribute, and field names or
TableGroupBy objects in the property. Not applied to a `dataSource`, which only holds the rows it fetched.

members.name: groupDisplay
members.description: `row` gives each group a row of the grid with its column aggregates; `band` draws a full-width band per group.

members.name: expandedGroups
members.description:
Keys of the open groups (`region=EMEA/status=Paid`). While unset, every group follows `groups-collapsed`; the
first toggle writes the full list here, so it can be read, stored and handed back. `;`-separated in the attribute.

members.name: groupsCollapsed
members.description: Starts every group closed while `expandedGroups` is unset.

members.name: renderGroup
members.description: Renders a group's label in place of its formatted value. The slot `group:<key>` wins over both.

members.name: emptyGroupLabel
members.description: Label of the group of rows whose value is empty. Unset, `No value` in the table's language.

type.text: { treeInputs: unknown[]; itemInputs: unknown[]; grouping: Grouping } | undefined

members.name: #echoSignature
members.description: Keys of the group rows stuck under the header at the last render, to re-render only when they change.

members.name: grouped
members.description: Whether the rows are currently grouped: `groupBy` names a level and the rows are the table's own.

members.name: getGroups
members.description: Every group, outermost first and each followed by its sub-groups, whether its parent is open or not.

members.name: expandGroup
members.description: Opens the group with `key`. Does not fire `group-toggle`, which reports what the user did.

members.name: collapseGroup
members.description: Closes the group with `key`.

members.name: expandAll
members.description: Opens every group.

members.name: collapseAll
members.description: Closes every group.

members.name: #renderGroupRow
members.description:
One group's row. `line` is its display line, or -1 for a copy stuck under the header ("echo"), which is hidden
from assistive technology — the real row is further up — holds nothing focusable, and toggles the real group.

members.name: #groupLevels
members.description: The grouping levels, normalized from `groupBy`; empty when the table is not grouped.

members.name: #grouping
members.description:
The group tree and the display list, or `undefined` when the rows are not grouped. Cached in two layers on their
inputs: the tree only depends on the rows and the levels, and opening a group should not re-bucket 10k rows.

members.name: #buildGroupTree
members.description:
Buckets `source` level by level. Rows keep their order inside a bucket; the buckets of a level are ordered by
their value, following the level's `sort`, else the direction the table is sorted by that field, else ascending.

members.name: #fieldColumn
members.description: The column definition showing `field`, hidden ones included: a grouped column is usually hidden, but formats the label.

members.name: #groupSummary
members.description: The column aggregates of a group's rows, keyed by column id; the same `summary` the totals row uses.

members.name: #groupAtLevel
members.description: The item on display line `line`: its group, or the group at `level` above it.

members.name: #depthOf
members.description: How many group levels a line sits under: the number of groups that can be stuck above it.

members.name: #pagePrefix
members.description:
Blank lines above a page that starts inside a group, where that group's headers are repeated. Every page counts
`pageSize` lines of its own; the repeated headers come on top.

members.name: #stuckGroups
members.description:
The groups whose own row has scrolled past the header (or sits on an earlier page) while lines of theirs are
still on screen, outermost first. They are drawn stuck under the header, one line per level, the way CSS sticky
would place them — the real rows cannot do it themselves, as the virtualizer drops them once off screen.

members.name: #measureHeaderHeight
members.description: Where the stuck group rows start: right under the header, whose height is themed.

members.name: orderRows
members.description: Sorts, then while grouped gathers the rows of each group together in the order of the groups.

members.name: structured
members.description: Whether the display lines are not simply the rows (groups, a tree): a `treegrid`, with no detail panels.

members.name: lineCount
members.description: Number of display lines across every page when they are not the rows; `undefined` for a flat table.

members.name: rowTotal
members.description:
How many rows the header checkbox counts against on a table that is not paginated: the rows on show, or while
grouped or in a tree every row, including those in closed groups and under closed rows.

members.name: rowIndexAt
members.description: The row index on display line `line`, or -1 for a line that is no data row (a group row).

members.name: lineOfRow
members.description: The display line of the row at `index`, or -1 while a closed group or parent hides it.

members.name: renderLine
members.description: A line that is no data row, such as a group row, drawn by the subclass; `undefined` draws the line's data row.

members.name: lineKey
members.description: The `repeat` key of a line that is no data row.

members.name: rowLevel
members.description: The place of the data row on line `line` in a hierarchy; `undefined` in a flat table.

members.name: renderAbove
members.description: Drawn between the header and the body: the group rows kept under the header.

members.name: onViewportScroll
members.description: The body scrolled; a subclass with rows kept under the header redraws them.

members.name: handleLineKey
members.description: Handles a key a hierarchy owns (the treegrid's ←/→, Enter on a group); `true` when it did.

members.name: scrollToStructuredLine
members.description: While grouped: below the header and the groups stuck under it, counting the repeated headers of a page.

members.name: lineInputs
members.description: What the page-scoped summary depends on beyond the rows: the display lines of a hierarchy.

members.name: hostAriaLabel
members.description:
The host's `aria-label`, observed so the grid inside the shadow root is named after it: the host is not the
grid, so a name set on it would otherwise name nothing.

members.name: hostAriaLabelledBy
members.description:
The host's `aria-labelledby`. ARIA cannot resolve a light-DOM id from inside the shadow root, so the referenced
elements' text is copied onto the grid instead, and `aria-labelledby` wins over `aria-label` as ARIA ranks them.

members.name: rows
members.description: The rows to display. An array in the property, JSON in the attribute.

members.name: columns
members.description: Column definitions, as an alternative to `c2-table-column` children. Children win when both are present.

members.name: rowKey
members.description:
Field holding the identity of a row — its key — used for selection, DOM reuse, animated updates and cell slots;
may be a dotted path. A key is always a string: `{ id: 7 }` has the key `"7"`. Without one (or where the field is
empty) a row's key is its position in the sorted dataset, which moves when the rows are sorted or replaced — so
a selection would move with it. Set it whenever rows can be selected.

members.name: getRowKey
members.description:
Computes a row's key when no single field holds it, such as a composite `` row => `${row.region}:${row.sku}` ``.
Wins over `row-key`; the result is turned into a string. Property only.

members.name: selection
members.description:
`single` selects one row at a time, `multiple` supports ⌘/ctrl-click and shift-click ranges. A click selects the
row alone; clicking the row that is already the whole selection clears it, and ⌘/ctrl-click or Space toggles one row.

members.name: checkboxSelection
members.description: Adds a leading checkbox column, pinned to the start.

members.name: value
members.description:
Keys of the selected rows (see `row-key`): an array in the property, `;`-separated in the attribute. Entries are
stored as strings, so `[1, 2]` selects the rows whose key field holds `1` and `2`. To select by row rather than
by key, use `selectRows()`.

members.name: sortModel
members.description: The sort, in priority order: `SortModel[]` in the property, `field:asc;other:desc` in the `sort` attribute.

members.name: multiSort
members.description: Lets shift-click add a column to the sort instead of replacing it.

members.name: sortable
members.description: Makes every column sortable; a column's own `sortable` still wins.

members.name: resizable
members.description: Columns are resizable by default; `resizable="false"` turns it off. A column's own `resizable` still wins.

members.name: stripe
members.description: Tints odd rows with `--c2-table__row__odd--background`.

members.name: animateUpdates
members.description: Smoothly interpolates changed finite numbers when `rows` is replaced. Rows are matched by `row-key`, or by index.

members.name: updateDuration
members.description: Duration of an animated rows update in milliseconds.

members.name: cellPart
members.description:
Returns extra part names for a body cell from its value and row, added beside `cell` so a stylesheet can reach
cells by state: `({ column, value }) => column.field === 'score' && value < 50 ? 'cell-failing' : undefined` and
`c2-table::part(cell-failing)`. A string (whitespace-separated names) or an array. Property only.

members.name: rowStyle
members.description: Returns inline styles for a row from its current data. Property only; animated updates pass the intermediate row.

members.name: rowPart
members.description:
Returns extra part names for a row from its current data, added beside `row` so a stylesheet can reach rows by
state: `({ row }) => row.status === 'failed' ? 'row-failed' : undefined` and `c2-table::part(row-failed)`. A string
(whitespace-separated names) or an array. Property only; animated updates pass the intermediate row.

members.name: highlightUpdates
members.description: Pulses changed row backgrounds: green for additions/increases, red for removals/decreases, blue otherwise.

members.name: updateHighlightField
members.description: Numeric field that determines whether a modified row highlights as increased or decreased. Defaults to its first changed number.

members.name: virtual
members.description: `auto` virtualizes past `virtual-threshold` rows; `always` and `never` force it. `wrap` overrides it with `never`.

members.name: wrap
members.description:
Wraps body cell text onto several lines: rows grow to their content (at least `--c2-table__row--height`) and cells
are top-aligned and no longer clipped. Rows of different heights cannot be windowed, so this turns virtualization
off — every row is rendered, whatever `virtual` says.

members.name: rowHeight
members.description: Row height in pixels used before the first row has been measured.

members.name: overscan
members.description: Rows rendered above and below the viewport while virtualizing.

members.name: virtualThreshold
members.description: Row count past which `virtual="auto"` starts windowing.

members.name: dataSource
members.description: Lazy row source used instead of `rows`; the table requests one block at a time as rows scroll into view.

members.name: blockSize
members.description: Number of rows the table asks a `dataSource` for at a time.

members.name: loading
members.description: Shows the loading state; implied while a `dataSource` resolves its first block.

members.name: error
members.description: Shows the error state with this message.

members.name: emptyMessage
members.description: Message shown when there are no rows.

members.name: page
members.description: The page on show, 1-based. Only meaningful while the table is `paginated`; clamped to `pageCount`.

members.name: pageSize
members.description:
Rows per page. `0` leaves paging off; a `c2-pagination` slotted into the `footer` sets it from its own
`page-size` when the table has none, which is what makes the nested form work with no configuration.
With `rows` the page is sliced in place; with a `dataSource` each page is one request.

members.name: summaryValues
members.description:
Values of the summary row keyed by column `id` (its `field` unless set), such as totals computed by a server.
An entry wins over the column's `summary` aggregate. An object in the property, JSON in the attribute.

members.name: summaryScope
members.description: Rows the summary aggregates cover: `all` rows, or only the `page` on show. A `dataSource` is only aggregated per page.

members.name: detailHeight
members.description:
Height in pixels of a row's detail panel, and the switch of the feature: above 0, every row gets a chevron that
opens a panel of this height under it. Declared, like `row-height`, so the rows stay windowed. `c2-group-table`
ignores it while its rows are grouped (`group-by`), and `c2-tree-table` while they are a tree (`children-field`).

members.name: renderDetail
members.description: Draws the detail panel of an open row. Unset, the panel shows the child in the row's `detail:{key}` slot.

members.name: expandedDetails
members.description: Keys of the rows whose detail panel is open, `;`-separated in the attribute. The table writes it as rows are opened and closed.

members.name: detailLabel
members.description: Accessible name of the chevron that opens a row's detail panel. Unset, `Details` in the table's language.

members.name: bulkSelect
members.description:
Adds a caret beside the header checkbox (`selection="multiple"` with `checkbox-selection`) that opens a menu: select
this page, select all N rows, or clear the selection. The checkbox itself selects the rows on show. Which of them
the user chose is `selectionScope`, and `selection-change` reports it as `scope`.

members.name: selectionScope
members.description:
How the current selection was made: `rows` one by one, `page` the page on show, `all` every row. With a
`dataSource`, `all` means every row the source holds, not only the keys in `value` (the loaded ones), and rows
that arrive later are drawn selected: act on the whole set server side. The table writes it with each selection.

members.name: filterable
members.description:
Adds a filter of its values to every column's header; a column's own `filterable` still wins. With a `dataSource`
a column lists the values of its `options`, and one without `options` gets no filter.

members.name: filters
members.description:
The column filters, keyed by column id: `{ "status": { "include": ["Paid"] } }`. A filterable column's header
writes it as the user picks values, and `filter-change` reports it. Applied on the client; with a `dataSource`
they go to `getRows` instead. An object in the property, JSON in the attribute.

members.name: baseline
members.description:
The rows to compare with, such as the last payroll run: matched by `row-key` (or `getRowKey`, one is needed), they give each column with
`compare` or `variance-threshold` its previous value. An array in the property, JSON in the attribute.

members.name: editable
members.description:
Lets the user edit the cells of the columns that have an `editor` (or a `renderEditor`): Enter, F2, a double click
or typing opens one editor over the cell, Enter or Tab commits it and moves on, Escape cancels, Delete clears the
cell, and a block copied from a spreadsheet pastes from the focused cell. Each change fires `cell-change` and
replaces `rows`. The editing code loads on the first edit. Not applied to a `dataSource`.

members.name: isCellEditable
members.description: Decides per cell whether an `editable` table lets it be edited, such as `({ row }) => row.status !== 'approved'`. Property only.

members.name: rowRule
members.description:
Adjusts a row after one of its cells is edited or pasted, before the table stores it: return the row to keep, such
as the debit cleared when a credit is typed, or a total recomputed from a quantity. Property only.

members.name: #pagers
members.description: The pagers that have announced themselves, so only their events are swallowed — not a pager inside a cell.

members.name: #animation
members.description: The realtime update code (`animate-updates`) once loaded, and its load while it is on the way.

members.name: #awaitAnimation
members.description: `rows` was replaced before that code arrived: the update waits for it rather than skip the animation.

type.text: { inputs: unknown[]; rows: TableRow[]; values: Map<string, unknown> } | undefined

members.name: #runningCache
members.default: new WeakMap<TableColumnConfig, { inputs: unknown[]; totals: Map<TableRow, number> }>()
members.description: The totals of each `running` column, by column key.

members.name: #blocksVersion
members.description: Counts the blocks a `dataSource` delivered, which is when a row of an open detail may appear.

members.name: #filter
members.description: The column filter popover once loaded, and its load while it is on the way.

type.text: { inputs: unknown[]; rows: Map<string, TableRow> } | undefined

members.name: #editing
members.description: The editing module once loaded (`editable`, `addRow`…), and its load while it is on the way.

members.name: #renderedRange
members.description: The window `range-change` last reported, to fire only when it moves.

members.name: #rangeReported
members.description: Whether `range-change` has fired yet: the first update reports even an empty window.

members.name: pager
members.description:
Shared with a `c2-pagination` slotted into the `footer`. Rebuilt rather than mutated whenever the paging state
moves: `@lit/context` consumers only re-render on a new object identity.

members.name: #virtualizer
members.default: new VirtualScrollController(this, { scrollElement: () => this.viewport, itemCount: () => this.rowCount, itemHeight: () => this.rowHeightPx, overscan: () => this.overscan, enabled: () => this.isVirtualized, })

members.name: totalRows
members.description: Total number of rows the table knows about: `rows.length`, or the `dataSource` total.

members.name: rowCount
members.description:
Number of rows on screen right now: the whole dataset, or one page of it while `paginated`. This is what the
virtualizer windows and what `virtual="auto"` measures, so a 25-row page is never virtualized against a
million-row total.

members.name: paginated
members.description:
Whether the table is paging its rows. `rows` are sliced in place; a `dataSource` is asked for one page per
request. Either way `page-size` is the switch, and a pager slotted into the `footer` sets it.

members.name: pageCount
members.description: Number of pages, at least 1.

members.name: #lineCount
members.description:
Lines the body is made of across every page: the rows, or while grouped the visible group and data rows. Pages
and `aria-rowcount` count these, so a collapsed group takes one line.

members.name: pageStart
members.description: Index of the first row of the current page within the whole dataset.

members.name: #effectiveBlockSize
members.description: A page is one block, so the existing block cache and request de-duplication carry paging unchanged.

members.name: isVirtualized
members.description: Whether the rows are currently windowed.

members.name: resolvedColumns
members.description: The resolved, ordered, visible columns — children first, then the `columns` property, then one per key of the first row.

members.name: sourceRows
members.description: The rows the table sorts, filters and draws: `rows`, or what a variant makes of its own input (`c2-flowsheet`).

members.name: keyOf
members.description:
The key of `row`: `getRowKey(row)`, else its `row-key` field, as a string. Without either it is the row's current
position, found by identity among the rows the table holds, and `undefined` when the row is not one of them.

members.name: isSelected
members.description: Whether `row` is selected.

members.name: #isKeySelected
members.description: Whether the row with `key` is selected: in `value`, or every row of a source after "select all" (`bulk-select`).

members.name: #allOfSource
members.description: "Select all" on a `dataSource` table with `bulk-select`: every row the source holds, loaded or not.

members.name: selectRows
members.description:
Selects `rows` by their keys, replacing the selection unless `add` is set; `selection="single"` keeps the last
one. Fires `selection-change`, like `selectAll()`. No-op while `selection="none"`.

members.name: deselectRows
members.description: Removes `rows` from the selection. Fires `selection-change`.

members.name: getSelectedRows
members.description: The rows currently selected, on every page. Only the loaded ones when a `dataSource` is used.

members.name: selectAll
members.description:
Selects every row, on every page. With a `dataSource` only the loaded rows have keys to select: `selectionScope`
becomes `all`, which tells the application the user meant every row the source holds, and with `bulk-select` the
rows that arrive later are drawn selected. No-op unless `selection="multiple"`.

members.name: selectPage
members.description:
Adds the rows on the page on show to the selection (every row while the table is not paginated), keeping the rows
selected on other pages. No-op unless `selection="multiple"`.

members.name: #deselectPage
members.description: Takes the rows on the page on show out of the selection, keeping those of other pages.

members.name: #selectedKeys
members.description: The selected keys as a list: `value`, or every loaded key while "select all" covers a source.

members.name: #pageKeys
members.description: The keys of the data rows on the page on show, groups and closed rows aside.

members.name: #forEachLoadedRow
members.description: Every row the table holds with its key: all of them on the client, the fetched blocks with a `dataSource`.

members.name: clearSelection
members.description: Clears the selection.

members.name: scrollToIndex
members.description:
Scrolls the row at `index` into view; while grouped or in a tree, only a row whose groups or parents are open has
a place to scroll to.

members.name: expandDetail
members.description: Opens the detail panel of the row with `key` (`detail-height`). Does not fire `detail-toggle`.

members.name: collapseDetail
members.description: Closes the detail panel of the row with `key`.

members.name: addRow
members.description:
Adds `row` at `index` (the end by default) of `rows`, as a new row of `getChanges()`, and fires `rows-change`.
Resolves to the row once it is drawn, so `scrollToIndex` can reach it.

members.name: duplicateRow
members.description:
Adds a copy of `row` under it, without its `row-key` field, with `overrides` written over it: pass the copy's new
key there when `getRowKey` builds keys. Resolves to the copy once it is drawn, or `undefined` when `row` is not a
top-level row.

members.name: deleteRows
members.description: Removes `rows` from `rows` (and from the children of a tree), and from the selection; fires `rows-change`.

members.name: #keepSelection
members.description:
Runs a change of the rows and keeps the selection on the same rows (less the `dropped` ones): without a `row-key`
a key is a position, which now points at another row. Fires `selection-change` only if the keys moved.

members.name: #selectableRows
members.description:
The rows whose selection survives a change: those on show, plus with a key the ones a filter hides (a selected row
stays selected while it is filtered out). Without a key a position is the key, so only the rows on show count.

members.name: getChanges
members.description: The rows added, edited and deleted since the rows were given or `acceptChanges()` ran.

members.name: acceptChanges
members.description: Takes the rows as they are as the new baseline, after a save: no cell is marked as changed any more.

members.name: revertChanges
members.description: Undoes every change since the baseline: edits, added and deleted rows. Fires `rows-change`.

members.name: validate
members.description: Checks every cell of the editable columns (`required`, the editor's type, `validate`), marks the invalid ones and resolves to them.

members.name: #canEdit
members.description: Whether the cell on display line `line` can be edited: an editable column, a data row, and `isCellEditable` agrees.

members.name: #beginEdit
members.description: Starts an edit of a cell once the editing module is in.

members.name: #handleEditGesture
members.description:
A double click on a cell, or a block pasted from a spreadsheet, in an editable table: handed to the editing module.
One listener each on the grid, so the cells carry none. The pasted text is read now: it is gone once the event ends.

members.name: buildRows
members.description: The rows the table shows, by index: `orderRows`, or in a subclass the flattened tree it builds.

members.name: childField
members.description: The field holding a row's child rows, or `''` without a tree.

members.name: isPartial
members.description: Whether row `key` shows the mixed state in its checkbox: some of the rows under it are selected.

members.name: cascade
members.description: Turns row `key` on or off in `keys`; a tree takes the rows under it along.

members.name: selectRange
members.description: Adds the rows of a shift-click range to `keys`.

members.name: inSummary
members.description: Whether the row at `index` counts in the summary row and a running total: in a tree, only the leaves do.

members.name: hiddenAutoField
members.description: A field of the first row the automatic columns leave out: a tree's children field.

members.name: displayRows
members.description: The rows as the application gave them, in display order: the update's transition rows while one animates.

members.name: refresh
members.description: Drops the `dataSource` cache and reloads the visible rows.

members.name: goToPage
members.description: Shows `page`, clamped to the available range, and loads it. Fires `page-change` when the page actually moves.

members.name: setPageSize
members.description: Changes the rows per page, keeping the first row of the current page on screen.

members.name: renderedRange
members.description:
The body rows rendered by the last update: their display lines, the keys of their data rows and `rows`, one
`{ line, key, row }` entry per rendered data row. While the table virtualizes this is the window, so a framework
filling `cell-slot` columns needs light-DOM children only for those lines (`slot="cell:{line}:{field}"`).
`range-change` fires whenever it changes.

members.name: focusLine
members.description: Moves the roving tabindex to a cell of display line `line` (a click on a group row, which does not select).

members.name: #renderRow
members.description: A data row on display line `line`, which is also its row index unless the rows are grouped.

members.name: #renderCell
members.description:
`line` is the cell's display line (focus, keyboard), `rowIndex` the row's index (data, keys). `level` is the row's
place in a hierarchy (a group, a tree), from `rowLevel`: its column holds the indentation and the chevron.

members.name: #versus
members.description:
A cell against the matching row of `baseline`: the change as `compare` shows it, and whether it passes the
column's `variance-threshold`. Nothing when either value is not a number.

members.name: #flagOf
members.description:
Where a cell stands against its row's `critical-range`, then its `reference-range`, and the mark it shows: the
short letter a lab report prints (`H`, `L`), its name for a screen reader and the range as its tooltip.

members.name: #limits
members.description: The two limits of a range attribute (`low,high`): each a number, or the field of the row that holds one.

members.name: cellDecoration
members.description:
What a body cell adds to its parts and after its content: the names `cellPart` returns, and what a variant adds
(`c2-allocation-grid` marks a week over capacity). Called for every rendered cell, so it stays cheap.

members.name: #isFilterable
members.description: Whether `column` has a filter in its header: its own `filterable`, else the table's.

members.name: #renderFilterButton
members.description: The filter button of a header: it opens the column's values, and shows when the column is filtered.

members.name: filterRows
members.description:
`rows` without those the column filters drop; `skip` leaves one column's filter out (its own value list shows the
values the other filters let through). Values compare as text. Not applied to a `dataSource`, which filters itself.

members.name: filterValueRows
members.description: The rows a column's filter counts its values over: those every other filter lets through.

members.name: filterTest
members.description: Whether a row passes every active filter (but `skip`'s); undefined when no filter is active.

members.name: #renderCheckCell
members.description: The checkbox of a `checkbox` column: toggled in place while the cell can be edited, a read-only mark otherwise.

members.name: #detail
members.description: Whether rows have a detail panel: `detail-height` is set and the rows are neither grouped nor a tree.

members.name: #detailLines
members.description:
The lines of the page whose detail panel is open, in order, counted from the page's first line. Found by one walk
over the rows, kept until the rows, the page or the open keys change: scrolling never repeats it.

members.name: #window
members.description:
The window to render: the virtualizer's, which counts uniform rows, moved by the detail panels open above it.
Each adds `detail-height` to the offset of the rows after it, so the first visible row is found by walking the
open panels, and the spacers carry the panels outside the window. With no panel open it is the virtualizer's own.

members.name: #renderDetailToggle
members.description: The chevron that opens a row's detail panel: a button, since a plain grid row has no expanded state of its own.

members.name: #renderDetailRow
members.description:
The panel under an open row: a row of the grid with one cell across every column, of the declared height. Its
cell is a tab stop, so a panel taller than its content's room scrolls from the keyboard. A renderer runs again
only when its row changes, so the panel keeps what the user did in it while the table redraws around it.

A closed panel filled from the row's slot stays in the page as `hidden="until-found"`, with no height, so
find-in-page reaches its text and opens it. Where the browser has no such state it is not drawn, and neither is
a renderer's panel, which is drawn on open.

members.name: #summaryCells
members.description: The summary row's cells: one per column, except that a `summary-span` cell stands in for the columns it covers.

members.name: #summaryData
members.description:
The rows the summary covers and the value of every column, keyed by column id. Cached on its inputs: the table
re-renders on every scroll frame while virtualizing, and aggregating a large dataset each time would be wasted.

members.name: formatAggregate
members.description:
A summary or group value as its cell shows it. A count is a number of rows, not an amount: a currency or date
column must not format it as one. A tally lists each value with its count, as a status where the column has them.

members.name: #renderStatus
members.description: A value of a `status` column: its mark, painted from its `options` entry, and its label.

members.name: cellValue
members.description:
The value of a cell: its field, or what a computed column makes of the row. `row` is the row as given, which
`running` totals are keyed by.

members.name: #statusColumns
members.description:
Every `status` column, hidden ones included: hiding a column changes what the table shows, not what a row's
`count-value` counts. Kept until the column definitions change.

members.name: #runningTotals
members.description:
A `running` column's total after each row, accumulated once over the rows in their sorted order whenever they or
the column change. Not computed for a `dataSource`, which only holds the rows it has fetched.

members.name: #rowAt
members.description: `index` is the row's position in the whole dataset, on every page.

members.name: #sourceRowAt
members.description: The row at `index` as the application gave it: `#rowAt` without the interpolation of an animated update.

members.name: identityOf
members.description: The key a row carries itself, from `getRowKey` or `row-key`; `undefined` when it has none and only its position identifies it.

members.name: #warnPositionalKeys
members.description: A selectable table without a key selects positions, which re-point at other rows after a sort. Say so, once.

members.name: scrollToLine
members.description: Scrolls display line `line` into view, below the header and, while grouped, below the groups stuck under it.

members.name: sortBySortModel

type.text: (item: T, field: string, column?: TableColumnConfig) => unknown

members.description: Sorts rows, or tree nodes, by `sortModel`; `read` reads an item's value in a column (a tree node's rollup).

members.name: focus
members.description:
Moves focus to the cell holding the roving tabindex — where Tab would land — so an app can hand focus back to the
table, e.g. after a bulk action hides the control that had it. Before the first render it focuses that cell once
it exists.

members.name: #handleColumnChange
members.description: A column definition changed one of its own properties: re-read them all, keeping the event inside the table.

members.name: #handlePagerConnect
members.description:
A pager connected somewhere inside the table. Adopt its page size when the table has none, so the nested form
needs no configuration, and keep the event inside the table.

members.name: #handlePagerEvent
members.description:
A pager the table drives re-emits what it just asked for, so the table swallows it and answers with its own
event — one `page-change` leaves the table, not two. Three things must still get through: the table's own event
(it fires this listener at-target), a `c2-pagination` used inside a cell renderer, and any pager on a table that
is not paging, which the author is wiring up by hand.

members.name: gridLabel
members.description:
The grid's accessible name: the host's `aria-labelledby` (the text of the elements it names, looked up in the
host's own tree) first, as ARIA ranks it, then the host's `aria-label`.

members.name: #activateRow
members.description: Fires `row-activate`. Not bubbling, like `selection-change`: a table nested in a cell must not open the outer row.

members.name: #handleContextMenuRequest
members.description: An enclosing `c2-context-menu` asks what was right-clicked: the cell, with the same detail as `cell-click`.

members.name: #headerSelection
members.description: What the header checkbox shows: every row on show selected, or some of them.

members.name: #renderBulkButton
members.description: The caret beside the header checkbox: a menu of this page, every row and none, loaded on first use.

members.name: #applySelection
members.description: `line` is a display line; a range covers the data rows on the lines between the anchor and it.

members.name: #isFromCellControl
members.description:
Whether a key comes from a control inside a cell — a slotted button, a `renderCell` input, the row checkbox —
rather than from the cell itself. Enter and Space belong to that control (cancelling them here used to stop a
slotted button from ever activating from the keyboard), and so does every key while it edits text.

members.name: footerHeight
members.description: Height of the summary row, which stays at the bottom of the viewport and covers the rows under it.

members.name: #syncFocusToWindow
members.description: Keeps the roving tabindex on a rendered cell: follows the window when focused, falls back to the header otherwise.

attributes.name: readings-field
attributes.description: The field of each row holding its readings by time, and of the `c2-table-column` that is the time columns' template.

attributes.name: observations
attributes.description:
Readings as a flat list, sorted into the rows by `measure` (a row's key) and `time`. A reading of a measure no
row has is left out. An array in the property, JSON in the attribute.

attributes.name: times
attributes.description: Times shown even with no reading yet, `;`-separated in the attribute: the column of the next round.

attributes.name: time-order
attributes.description: `asc` (the default) puts the earliest time first, `desc` the newest.

attributes.name: time-format
attributes.description: How the headers write the times: `time` (the default, with the day over the first time of each day), `date`, `datetime` or `text`.

attributes.name: group-by
attributes.description:
Groups the rows by these fields, outermost first: `group-by="region,status"` in the attribute, and field names or
TableGroupBy objects in the property. Not applied to a `dataSource`, which only holds the rows it fetched.

attributes.name: group-display
attributes.description: `row` gives each group a row of the grid with its column aggregates; `band` draws a full-width band per group.

attributes.name: expanded-groups
attributes.description:
Keys of the open groups (`region=EMEA/status=Paid`). While unset, every group follows `groups-collapsed`; the
first toggle writes the full list here, so it can be read, stored and handed back. `;`-separated in the attribute.

attributes.name: groups-collapsed
attributes.description: Starts every group closed while `expandedGroups` is unset.

attributes.name: empty-group-label
attributes.description: Label of the group of rows whose value is empty. Unset, `No value` in the table's language.

attributes.name: aria-label
attributes.description:
The host's `aria-label`, observed so the grid inside the shadow root is named after it: the host is not the
grid, so a name set on it would otherwise name nothing.

attributes.name: aria-labelledby
attributes.description:
The host's `aria-labelledby`. ARIA cannot resolve a light-DOM id from inside the shadow root, so the referenced
elements' text is copied onto the grid instead, and `aria-labelledby` wins over `aria-label` as ARIA ranks them.

attributes.name: rows
attributes.description: The rows to display. An array in the property, JSON in the attribute.

attributes.name: columns
attributes.description: Column definitions, as an alternative to `c2-table-column` children. Children win when both are present.

attributes.name: row-key
attributes.description:
Field holding the identity of a row — its key — used for selection, DOM reuse, animated updates and cell slots;
may be a dotted path. A key is always a string: `{ id: 7 }` has the key `"7"`. Without one (or where the field is
empty) a row's key is its position in the sorted dataset, which moves when the rows are sorted or replaced — so
a selection would move with it. Set it whenever rows can be selected.

attributes.name: selection
attributes.description:
`single` selects one row at a time, `multiple` supports ⌘/ctrl-click and shift-click ranges. A click selects the
row alone; clicking the row that is already the whole selection clears it, and ⌘/ctrl-click or Space toggles one row.

attributes.name: checkbox-selection
attributes.description: Adds a leading checkbox column, pinned to the start.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description:
Keys of the selected rows (see `row-key`): an array in the property, `;`-separated in the attribute. Entries are
stored as strings, so `[1, 2]` selects the rows whose key field holds `1` and `2`. To select by row rather than
by key, use `selectRows()`.

attributes.name: sort
attributes.description: The sort, in priority order: `SortModel[]` in the property, `field:asc;other:desc` in the `sort` attribute.

attributes.name: multi-sort
attributes.description: Lets shift-click add a column to the sort instead of replacing it.

attributes.name: sortable
attributes.description: Makes every column sortable; a column's own `sortable` still wins.

attributes.name: resizable
attributes.description: Columns are resizable by default; `resizable="false"` turns it off. A column's own `resizable` still wins.

attributes.name: stripe
attributes.description: Tints odd rows with `--c2-table__row__odd--background`.

attributes.name: animate-updates
attributes.description: Smoothly interpolates changed finite numbers when `rows` is replaced. Rows are matched by `row-key`, or by index.

attributes.name: update-duration
attributes.description: Duration of an animated rows update in milliseconds.

attributes.name: highlight-updates
attributes.description: Pulses changed row backgrounds: green for additions/increases, red for removals/decreases, blue otherwise.

attributes.name: update-highlight-field
attributes.description: Numeric field that determines whether a modified row highlights as increased or decreased. Defaults to its first changed number.

attributes.name: virtual
attributes.description: `auto` virtualizes past `virtual-threshold` rows; `always` and `never` force it. `wrap` overrides it with `never`.

attributes.name: wrap
attributes.description:
Wraps body cell text onto several lines: rows grow to their content (at least `--c2-table__row--height`) and cells
are top-aligned and no longer clipped. Rows of different heights cannot be windowed, so this turns virtualization
off — every row is rendered, whatever `virtual` says.

attributes.name: row-height
attributes.description: Row height in pixels used before the first row has been measured.

attributes.name: overscan
attributes.description: Rows rendered above and below the viewport while virtualizing.

attributes.name: virtual-threshold
attributes.description: Row count past which `virtual="auto"` starts windowing.

attributes.name: block-size
attributes.description: Number of rows the table asks a `dataSource` for at a time.

attributes.name: loading
attributes.description: Shows the loading state; implied while a `dataSource` resolves its first block.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Shows the error state with this message.

attributes.name: empty-message
attributes.description: Message shown when there are no rows.

attributes.name: page
attributes.description: The page on show, 1-based. Only meaningful while the table is `paginated`; clamped to `pageCount`.

attributes.name: page-size
attributes.description:
Rows per page. `0` leaves paging off; a `c2-pagination` slotted into the `footer` sets it from its own
`page-size` when the table has none, which is what makes the nested form work with no configuration.
With `rows` the page is sliced in place; with a `dataSource` each page is one request.

attributes.name: summary-values
attributes.description:
Values of the summary row keyed by column `id` (its `field` unless set), such as totals computed by a server.
An entry wins over the column's `summary` aggregate. An object in the property, JSON in the attribute.

attributes.name: summary-scope
attributes.description: Rows the summary aggregates cover: `all` rows, or only the `page` on show. A `dataSource` is only aggregated per page.

attributes.name: detail-height
attributes.description:
Height in pixels of a row's detail panel, and the switch of the feature: above 0, every row gets a chevron that
opens a panel of this height under it. Declared, like `row-height`, so the rows stay windowed. `c2-group-table`
ignores it while its rows are grouped (`group-by`), and `c2-tree-table` while they are a tree (`children-field`).

attributes.name: expanded-details
attributes.description: Keys of the rows whose detail panel is open, `;`-separated in the attribute. The table writes it as rows are opened and closed.

attributes.name: detail-label
attributes.description: Accessible name of the chevron that opens a row's detail panel. Unset, `Details` in the table's language.

attributes.name: bulk-select
attributes.description:
Adds a caret beside the header checkbox (`selection="multiple"` with `checkbox-selection`) that opens a menu: select
this page, select all N rows, or clear the selection. The checkbox itself selects the rows on show. Which of them
the user chose is `selectionScope`, and `selection-change` reports it as `scope`.

attributes.name: selection-scope
attributes.description:
How the current selection was made: `rows` one by one, `page` the page on show, `all` every row. With a
`dataSource`, `all` means every row the source holds, not only the keys in `value` (the loaded ones), and rows
that arrive later are drawn selected: act on the whole set server side. The table writes it with each selection.

attributes.name: filterable
attributes.description:
Adds a filter of its values to every column's header; a column's own `filterable` still wins. With a `dataSource`
a column lists the values of its `options`, and one without `options` gets no filter.

attributes.name: filters
attributes.description:
The column filters, keyed by column id: `{ "status": { "include": ["Paid"] } }`. A filterable column's header
writes it as the user picks values, and `filter-change` reports it. Applied on the client; with a `dataSource`
they go to `getRows` instead. An object in the property, JSON in the attribute.

attributes.name: baseline
attributes.description:
The rows to compare with, such as the last payroll run: matched by `row-key` (or `getRowKey`, one is needed), they give each column with
`compare` or `variance-threshold` its previous value. An array in the property, JSON in the attribute.

attributes.name: editable
attributes.description:
Lets the user edit the cells of the columns that have an `editor` (or a `renderEditor`): Enter, F2, a double click
or typing opens one editor over the cell, Enter or Tab commits it and moves on, Escape cancels, Delete clears the
cell, and a block copied from a spreadsheet pastes from the focused cell. Each change fires `cell-change` and
replaces `rows`. The editing code loads on the first edit. Not applied to a `dataSource`.

slots.description: Label of one group, e.g. `slot="group:region=EMEA"`, in place of its formatted value and row count. The copy of the group kept under the header while its rows scroll shows the built-in label.
slots.name: group:{groupKey}

slots.description: The column definitions: `c2-table-column` elements. They render nothing themselves.
slots.name: default

slots.description: Bar above the header, for a title, filters or a column menu. Hidden when empty.
slots.name: toolbar

slots.description: Bar below the rows, for a row count or a `c2-pagination`. Hidden when empty.
slots.name: footer

slots.description: Replaces the built-in "no rows" message.
slots.name: empty

slots.description: Replaces the built-in spinner shown while the first rows load.
slots.name: loading

slots.description: Replaces the built-in message shown when `error` is set.
slots.name: error

slots.description: Meaningful server-rendered table content. It remains visible before custom-element upgrade and is retained in the light DOM but hidden after the interactive grid mounts, avoiding duplicate client content.
slots.name: fallback

slots.description: Detail panel of one row (`detail-height`), e.g. `slot="detail:ORD-7"`, shown while that row is open and `renderDetail` is unset.
slots.name: detail:{key}

slots.description: Body of one cell of a column marked `cell-slot`, e.g. `slot="cell:0:change"` for the first displayed row. `line` is the cell's display line, counted across the whole dataset after sort, filter and grouping with the page offset included — the numbering of `range-change`. Lets a framework render a cell with its own template language instead of a `renderCell` function; the column's `renderCell` or formatted value stays as the fallback. Children are needed only for the lines `range-change` reports (map `detail.rows`, or `renderedRange.rows`, each `{ line, key, row }`); a child whose line is outside the rendered window is left unassigned. After a sort, filter or page change the same line holds a different row, so re-render the children from the next `range-change`.
slots.name: cell:{line}:{field}

events.name: group-toggle
events.description: Fired after the user opens or closes a group, with its `key`, whether it is now `expanded`, and the `group` itself (its rows and aggregates). `expandedGroups` already holds the new state. Does not bubble.

events.name: page-change
events.description: Fired after the shown page changes, while `paginated`. `detail.start` and `detail.count` are the slice of the whole dataset now shown — with a `dataSource`, the `getRows` request that follows. A pager slotted in the footer does not fire its own: the table speaks for it.

events.name: range-change
events.description: Fired after the rendered body rows change — the window scrolled, or the rows, sort, page or grouping changed. `detail.start`/`detail.end` are the display lines rendered (end exclusive), `detail.rows` one `{ line, key, row }` entry per rendered data row in display order (group rows and rows a `dataSource` has not delivered are left out) and `detail.keys` their keys. Those lines are the only ones whose `cell:{line}:{field}` slots exist. Fires again when the same keys move to other lines. Does not bubble.

events.name: sort-change
events.description: Fired after the user clicks a sortable header. `detail.sort` is the new sort model, in priority order.

events.name: detail-toggle
events.description: Fired after the user opens or closes a row's detail panel (`detail-height`), with its `key`, the `row` and whether it is now open. Does not bubble.

events.name: row-click
events.description: Fired when a row is clicked, before the selection is applied.

events.name: row-activate
events.description: Fired when the user opens a row: a pointer click on it, or Enter on one of its focused cells — so one listener serves a table used for navigation from the mouse and the keyboard alike. Not fired by a click or Enter that belongs to a control inside a cell (a button, link or input), and fired before the selection is applied. Does not bubble: a table nested in another table's cell would otherwise open the outer row too, so the listener belongs on the element itself.

events.name: cell-click
events.description: Fired when a cell is clicked; adds `detail.column` and `detail.value`.

events.name: selection-change
events.description: Fired after the user changes the selection. `detail.value` is the array of selected row keys, `detail.rows` the matching rows, `detail.scope` how they were chosen (`rows`, `page`, `all`). Does not bubble: several components fire `selection-change`, so a listener belongs on the element itself rather than on an ancestor.

events.name: column-resize
events.description: Fired when the user releases a column's resize handle.

Fired when the user commits a new value to a cell of an `editable` table (typed, toggled, cleared or pasted), before the table stores it: `detail.row` is the row as it was, with `key`, `column`, `field`, `value` and `previousValue`. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps the old value. Does not bubble.
events.name: cell-change

events.description: Fired after the user changes a column's filter. `detail.filters` is every column's filter, as `filters` now holds them, and `detail.column` the id of the column that changed.
events.name: filter-change

events.description: Fired after the table replaced `rows` itself: a cell edited or pasted, a row added, duplicated or deleted, changes reverted. `detail.rows` is the new array and `detail.reason` says why. Does not bubble.
events.name: rows-change

declarations.description:
`c2-table` with nested rows: the same grid, columns, sorting, selection, pinning, windowing, paging, summary row,
editing and realtime updates, plus rows nested to any depth (`children-field`). Every attribute, property, event,
part and CSS variable of `c2-table` works here as well; what follows is what the tree adds. Use `c2-table` when the
rows are flat and `c2-group-table` to gather flat rows into groups: each leaves this code out.

`children-field="children"` reads each row's child rows from that field, nested to any depth, and the grid becomes a
`treegrid`: every row is a row of the grid, and the first column (or the one marked `group-column`) gets a chevron
and an indentation per level. Rows open with a click on the chevron, ←/→ on that column, `expandRow()` or
`expanded-rows` (the keys of the open rows; all closed until then, or open with `tree-expanded`), and `row-toggle`
reports a click. Sorting orders each level among its siblings, and a filter keeps a row that passes it with the
rows above it. A column with `rollup="sum"` (or `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`, or a function) shows in a parent row
the aggregate of the leaf rows under it, and the summary row counts leaves only. With `selection="multiple"` a row
is selected with the rows under it, and a parent is selected when all its children are; its checkbox shows the
mixed state in between. A row whose field holds `true` loads its children from `loadChildren` when it first opens.
Give the rows a `row-key`. The tree is built on the client and does not apply to a `dataSource`.

```html
<c2-tree-table row-key="id" children-field="children" tree-expanded>
  <c2-table-column field="name" header="Account"></c2-table-column>
  <c2-table-column field="amount" format="currency" align="end" rollup="sum"></c2-table-column>
</c2-tree-table>
```

cssProperties.description: Height of the resting divider, as a share of the header.
cssProperties.name: --c2-table__resizer--height

cssProperties.description: The divider drawn at a resizable column's edge.
